newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges trade higher, cargoes quiet.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges trade higher, cargoes quiet.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges traded quietly at higher numbers early on Friday, with one player rumoured to be trying to bid up the market to fetch a higher price for its own material, traders said.

High sulphur barges were done early at $86 a tonne fob Rotterdam but rose later to trade three times at $87 a tonne -- some $1 to $2 over Thursday's levels. Later bids were $86.50/$87 while offers were $87.50 a tonne.
Traders said bunker demand was light, with some putting it at about 10,000 tonnes and others citing lower numbers.
"Demand is not too high. Some 10,000 tonnes this morning but then Friday is not bunker day," one trader said.
One trader said a buyer bid the high numbers "to push up the prices so they can sell their own product higher".
High sulphur cargoes were still quiet with two cargoes of bunker grade material being offered at $79 and $81 fob respectively, but few buyers were seen.
